declared.title: Synthesizing the effects of mental simulation on behavior change: Systematic review and multilevel meta-analysis
declared.foundIn: OpenAlex search « mental simulation process outcome meta-analysis » (2026-11-23)

population: 94 experiments (123 effect sizes, N = 5,685) comparing mental simulation with a control group; mostly young students

findings.text: Mentally simulating a future behaviour improved that behaviour compared with control conditions

support.sentence: After applying a multilevel random effects model, a statistically-reliable positive effect of Hedges' g = 0.49, 95% CI [0.37; 0.62] was found, which was significantly different than zero.

findings.text: Imagining a desired, successful outcome improved later behaviour a little compared with control (15 effect sizes)

support.sentence: Thus, it is apparent here that simulation of superior outcomes (and positive simulations in general) is among several beneficial mental simulation subtypes which can be used as behavior change techniques.
support.readBy: choose-your-struggle agent, 2026-11-23: published PDF, ray.yorksj.ac.uk/4802, Discussion and Table 3

findings.text: Simulating the steps alone (5 effect sizes) had no reliable effect compared with control; the authors warn against strong claims for it

support.sentence: However, results from this meta-analysis show that caution is needed in making any strong assumptions about process simulations, at least until further empirical research conclusively replicates positive effects following process simulations.
support.readBy: choose-your-struggle agent, 2026-11-23: published PDF, ray.yorksj.ac.uk/4802, Discussion and Table 3

limits: the omnibus test of subtypes was not significant: subtype estimates are exploratory, some on very few studies (process: 5)
each subtype is compared with control groups, never process against outcome head to head
almost all participants were young students; behaviour mostly measured within a day of the simulation
countries not listed; no sample from the Middle East or North Africa known
